extracted.intended_audience: Users/developers of PARI/GP doing algebraic number theory computations (number fields, ideals, valuations, HNF, discrete log, etc.)
extracted.subtask_description: API reference for PARI/GP routines operating on number fields and ideals (ideal arithmetic, factorization, HNF, valuations, reductions, discrete logs, basis conversion, discriminants, compositums, etc.). Each entry documents function purpose, arguments, flags, return formats, examples and performance/usage notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealappr
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a fractional ideal x (in any form) return an element α in nf with vp(α)=vp(x) for primes where x has non-zero valuation, and vp(α) ≥ 0 elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: x may be given as a prime-ideal factorization (allowing zero exponents) to obtain α with exact valuations at primes occurring in x. The optional flag argument is deprecated/ignored. Use idealappr(nf,x). Library syntax: idealappr0(nf,x,flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealchinese
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve Chinese remainder type problem: given x as a prime-ideal factorization and y a vector of local targets, compute b with vp(b - y_p) ≥ vp(x) for primes in x and vp(b) ≥ 0 elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: x can be [x,s] to impose sign conditions at real embeddings (s components in {-1,0,1}); when y omitted returns an initialized data structure usable to accelerate many solves (idealchineseinit). Examples show speedups when reusing initialization. Library syntax: idealchinese(nf,x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealcoprime
rubrics_metrics.description: Given integral ideals x and y, return β in nf such that β·x is coprime to y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: idealcoprime(nf,x,y). No flags described.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealdiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute quotient x·y^{-1} of two ideals; result in HNF. Optional flag=non-zero indicates quotient assumed integral for faster algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag non-zero can be much faster when norm of quotient is small even though norms of x and y are large; algorithm cheaply removes maximal ideals above rational primes where vp(N x)=vp(N y). Library variants: idealdiv0(nf,x,y,flag), idealdiv(nf,x,y) (flag=0), idealdivexact(nf,x,y) (flag=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealfactor
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor an ideal x into prime ideal powers in the number field nf; output format similar to factor, primes represented as in idealprimedec. Optional lim restricts to primes above rational primes < lim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example showing factorization and limiting by rational primes. Library syntax: gpidealfactor(nf,x,lim) (for gp interface). Use idealfactor(GEN x) or idealfactor_limit(GEN x, ulong lim).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealfactorback
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a factorization f (and optional exponents e) return the corresponding ideal; integer 1 corresponds to empty factorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If e present, f and e must have same length and return product of f[i]^e[i]; if f is vector and e omitted, assume exponents 1. If f is a regular factorization as produced by idealfactor, reconstruct ideal. Optional flag non-zero performs ideal reductions (idealred) along the way—useful when ideals are extended to preserve principal parts. Library syntax: idealfactorback(nf,f,e,flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealfrobenius
rubrics_metrics.description: For Galois number field K with gal (galoisinit), and an unramified prime pr, return permutation of gal.group defining Frobenius element Frob_pr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pr is unique prime above rational p, then Frob acts as x -> x^p mod pr. Example: cyclotomic field, 101 ≡ 8 mod 31 so Frobenius=power 8. Library syntax: idealfrobenius(nf,gal,pr).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealhnf
rubrics_metrics.description: Return Hermite normal form (HNF) of ideal uZK + vZK where u and v are elements of K defined by nf. If v omitted, returns HNF of ideal defined by u (u may be algebraic number, maximal ideal, or matrix of generators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fewer than [K:Q] generators given, they define a ZK-module; if >= degree, assumed a Z-basis and acts like mathnf. Special handling for quadratic u given as Qfb(a,b,c) when discriminant matches. Errors if discriminant mismatch. Library syntax: idealhnf0(nf,u,v) and idealhnf(nf,a).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealintersect
rubrics_metrics.description: Intersection of two ideals A and B in nf; result given in HNF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not apply to general Z-modules (orders) since arguments are replaced by ideals they generate. Script given to intersect Z-modules via kernels and mathnf. Library syntax: idealintersect(nf,A,B).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealinv
rubrics_metrics.description: Inverse of ideal x in nf, given in HNF. If x is extended ideal [I,t] invert yields [I^{-1},1/t].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: idealinv(nf,x).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealispower
rubrics_metrics.description: Return 1 if fractional ideal A is an n-th power (A = B^n) and 0 otherwise; optional &B set to the n-th root in HNF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows call with &B returning B. Library syntax: idealispower(nf,A,n,&B).

rubrics_metrics.name: ideallist
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute list of all ideals of norm ≤ bound in nf. Result is a row vector with bound components; each component is a row vector of ideals of that norm; content depends on flag (0..4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag meanings: 0 give bid attached to ideals without generators; 1 include generators; 2 nf must be bnf with units and returns [bid,U] with unit discrete logs (for bnrclassnolist); 3 as 2 but include generators; 4 give only HNF of ideal (default). Examples show how to inspect clgp and mod data. Library syntax: ideallist0(nf,bound,flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: ideallistarch
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ideallist output and arch (Archimedean part), return vector of vectors with same structure but arch added to moduli info; preserves same flag format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to add places at infinity to moduli; example shows adding two infinite places increases (ZK/f)^* by copies of Z/2Z and changes class group structures. Library syntax: ideallistarch(nf,list,arch).

rubrics_metrics.name: ideallog
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute discrete logarithm of x with respect to generators given in bid (output of idealstar), assuming x has valuation 0 at primes in support of D; returns vector of exponents xi with 0 ≤ xi < di and x ≡ prod g_i^{xi} (mod *D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When nf omitted, take Q: then x must be integer and bid initialized by znstar(N,1). See znlog for limitations of discrete log algorithms when Archimedean places present. Library syntax: ideallog(nf=NULL,x,bid) and Zideallog when nf NULL.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealmin (deprecated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated function kept for backward compatibility: computes a pseudo-minimum of ideal x in direction vdir; advice to use idealred instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: vdir should be nf.r1 + nf.r2 component vector of non-negative integers; generally useless. Library syntax: idealmin(nf,ix,vdir).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealmul
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiply ideals x and y in nf; result is HNF. If operands are extended ideals [I,t], principal parts are updated accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show extended * ideal and extended * extended behavior. If flag non-zero, reduce result using idealred. Library variants: idealmul0(nf,x,y,flag), idealmul(nf,x,y) (flag=0), idealmulred(nf,x,y) (flag!=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealnorm
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute norm of ideal x in nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: idealnorm(nf,x).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealnumden
rubrics_metrics.description: Return [A,B] where A,B are coprime integer ideals such that x = A/B in nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: idealnumden((x+1)/2) returns numerator and denominator ideals. Library syntax: idealnumden(nf,x).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealpown
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute k-th power of ideal x (k ∈ Z); if x is extended [I,t], principal part updated to [I^k, t^k].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag non-zero, reduce result using idealred throughout powering process (not same as powering then reducing). Library syntax: idealpow0(nf,x,k,flag) and convenience variants idealpow and idealpows; idealpowred corresponds to flag=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealprimedec
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute prime ideal decomposition of rational prime p in nf; returns vector of prid structures pr = [p,a,e,f,mb] describing prime ideals above p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If f present and non-zero, restrict to primes of residue degree ≤ f. Components accessible as pr.p, pr.e, pr.f, pr.gen. Algebraic integer a guaranteed to have valuation 1 at the prime when e>1. Library syntax: idealprimedec_limit_f(nf,p,f).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealprincipalunits
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a prime ideal pr (in prid format) and integer k, return multiplicative group (1+pr)/(1+pr^k) as abelian group; faster than idealstar for large residue norm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned structure contains cyc (elementary divisors) and gen (minimal generators of given orders). Library syntax: idealprincipalunits(nf,pr,k).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealramgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: For Galois K/Q with gal and prime pr, return vector g of subgroups: g[1]=decomposition group, g[2]=inertia G0(P), and for i≥2 g[i]=G_{i-2}(P) ramification groups; length equals number of non-trivial groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows computing cardinalities. Can be used to find fixed fields of inertia groups and check ramification. Library syntax: idealramgroups(nf,gal,pr).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealred
rubrics_metrics.description: LLL-reduction of ideal I in nf along optional direction v; finds a ∈ K* such that J=(a)I is 'small' and integral; returns HNF of J. Preferred over idealmin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: v is vector of length nf.r1 + nf.r2 of non-negative integers; relative magnitudes matter. Often yields unit ideal if principal; not a guaranteed principality test—bnfisprincipal is the guaranteed test. For extended ideals [I,s] returns [J,sa] keeping track of principal part. Technical note: reduction approximates minimizing quadratic form ||·||_v (rescaled/rounded variant used). Changing directions randomizes output useful in index calculus algorithms. Library syntax: idealred0(nf,I,v).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealredmodpower
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ideal x and positive integer n, return b such that x * b^n = v is small; if x integral then v integral. Uses B-smooth factorization strategy to avoid full factorization up to B (primelimit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm factors out primes ≤ B to write x = I J^n with I B-smooth and returns small element in J^{-1}. B parameter avoids costly complete factorization; examples compare reductions modulo different powers and norms. Library syntax: idealredmodpower(nf,x,n,B).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealstar
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a bid structure necessary for computing in finite abelian group G = (Z_K/N)^*. bid contains mod, clgp, no, cyc, gen. Flag controls inclusion of generators and initialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag meanings: 1 (default) bid without generators (saves time); 2 include generators; 0 output only group as [h,d,g]. When nf omitted, N is integer and routine returns structure for (Z/NZ)^* (short for idealstar(nfinit(x),N,flag)). Alternative znstar exists with different default flag behavior. Better to use Idealstar with symbolic flag constants nf_GEN and nf_INIT rather than numeric flags. Library syntax: idealstar0(nf=NULL,N,flag) and Idealstar(nf,ideal,flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealtwoelt
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a two-element representation [a,α] of ideal x such that x = a Z_K + α Z_K (a chosen as positive generator of x∩Z unless x principal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When called with explicit a (non-zero) the function assumes a ∈ x and returns α with x = a Z_K + α Z_K; this requires factoring a and is generally slower and gives larger generators. Result is not recognized as an ideal by GP functions—use idealhnf to recover ideal structure. Library syntax: idealtwoelt0(nf,x,a) and convenience wrappers idealtwoelt and idealtwoelt2.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealval
rubrics_metrics.description: Give valuation of ideal x at prime pr (pr in idealprimedec format); valuation of 0 ideal is +∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available gp wrapper gpidealval and long idealval which returns LONG_MAX for x=0 and valuation as long. Library syntax: gpidealval(nf,x,pr) and idealval(nf,x,pr).

rubrics_metrics.name: matalgtobasis (deprecated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated: apply nfbasistoalg to each entry of a vector or matrix x; use apply instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: matalgtobasis(nf,x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matbasistoalg (deprecated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated: apply nfalgtobasis to each entry of a vector or matrix x; use apply instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: matbasistoalg(nf,x).

rubrics_metrics.name: modreverse
rubrics_metrics.description: Given z = Mod(A,T) a polmod with minimal polynomial Q of same degree as T, return Mod(B,Q) which is a reverse polmod (a root of T).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to change generating element in algebraic extensions and to convert between representations. Fails if minimal polynomial of z has lower degree than expected (domain error). Library syntax: modreverse(z). Examples illustrate computing alternate defining polynomials and explicit isomorphisms between representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: newtonpoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Return vector of slopes of Newton polygon of polynomial x with respect to prime p; components in decreasing order, vertical slopes denoted +∞ when constant coefficient zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: newtonpoly(x,p).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfalgtobasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Given algebraic number x in nf, transform it to column vector on integral basis nf.zk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inverse of nfbasistoalg. Examples show conversions for polynomial mods and basis vectors. Library syntax: algtobasis(nf,x).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfbasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Return an integral basis (Z-basis of maximal order) of number field defined by irreducible polynomial T with integer coefficients. Accepts optional listP to specify primes/integers for local maximality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses modified Round 4 algorithm. If discriminant factoring is hard, user can provide listP (vector of primes, factorization matrix, or integer B meaning primes ≤ B) to obtain basis maximal at those primes; the result is global integral basis if all prime divisors of field discriminant included. Examples show nfbasis([T,listP]) and interplay with nfinit and nfcertify. Composite integers allowed in listP if pairwise coprime; including composite C with C^2 | D may help. Library syntax: nfbasis(T,*d,listP=NULL) returning basis and order discriminant in *d.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfbasistoalg
rubrics_metrics.description: Transform algebraic number in nf from coordinate (basis) form to polmod (t_POLMOD) form; inverse of nfalgtobasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show conversions and behavior on Mod inputs. Library syntax: basistoalg(nf,x).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfcertify
rubrics_metrics.description: Given nf output by nfinit, check whether integer basis is known unconditionally; useful when nfinit used [T,listP] approximation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns vector of coprime composite integers; empty vector means nf.zk and nf.disc are correct. If non-empty, must factor the integers completely, addprime each prime factor, and re-check nfdisc. nfcertify automates/accelerates this process. Library syntax: nfcertify(nf).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfcompositum
rubrics_metrics.description: Given nf (field K) and squarefree polynomials P,Q in K[X], output simple factors R of etale K-algebra A = K[X,Y]/(P(X),Q(Y)); each factor R corresponds to K[X]/(R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More efficient if P,Q reduced to irreducible first. If inputs irreducible and linearly disjoint, there will be a single factor. Binary flag bits: 1 return vectors [R,a,b,k] giving expressions of roots and relation b + k a = X mod R; 2 assume P,Q define linearly disjoint fields and return single simple factor avoiding costly factorization over K. Variables of P/Q must have higher priority than nf (use varhigher/varlower). Examples show extracting compositum and reducing polynomial via rnfpolredbest. Library syntax: nfcompositum(nf,P,Q,flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfdetint
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a pseudo-matrix x, compute a non-zero ideal contained in (i.e., a multiple of) the determinant of x; useful with nfhnfmod.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: nfdetint(nf,x).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfdisc
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute field discriminant of number field defined by integral irreducible polynomial T using Round 4 algorithm. Accepts optional listP as in nfbasis to compute discriminant of an order maximal at specified primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When listP provided returns discriminant of order given by nfbasis(T,listP) with same valuations at primes in listP as field discriminant. Use padicdisc(T,p)=p^valuation(nfdisc(T,[p]),p) to get p-adic discriminant. Library syntax: nfdisc(T) and related nfbasis usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltadd
rubrics_metrics.description: Add two elements x and y in nf, returning their sum in nf representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows nfadd(1,x) producing [1,1]~ for 1+I. Library syntax: nfadd(nf,x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltdiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide two elements x and y in nf, returning x/y in nf representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: nfdiv(nf,x,y).
